findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
findings.body:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)`, line 483 checks:

```java
if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
```

There are two bugs here:
1. The encoded context prefix is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`), so the grant type shortcut is at indices `(4, 6)` (matching `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` line 81: `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`), not `(3, 5)`. `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type and the first character of the grant type.
2. The condition is not negated: it returns `false` when the substring *equals* `expectedGrantShortcut`, and only passes because `substring(3, 5)` never equals the expected grant shortcut. As a result, the matcher accepts any 5+ character prefix whose characters `[3..5)` do not equal `expectedGrantShortcut`, instead of verifying that `items[0]` has length 6 and ends with `expectedGrantShortcut`.

findings.title: Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body:
In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls:

```java
Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
```

It checks `grantType` a second time instead of checking `rawTokenId`. A `null` `rawTokenId` will therefore not be rejected at construction time and will instead be concatenated as the literal string `"null"` when `encodeTokenId` builds the token ID.

findings.title: Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() says 3-letters shortcut instead of 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` requires the entire encoded context (`sessionType + tokenType + grantType`) to be exactly 6 characters long (2 characters per field) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` if a grant type shortcut is not 2 characters.
